All Hilbert spaces in this item are nonzero and finite-dimensional over $\mathbb C$. A density operator $\rho$ on $H$ is a Hermitian positive semidefinite endomorphism with $\operatorname{Tr}\rho=1$. Its dimensionless von Neumann entropy, in nats, is

$$S(\rho):=-\operatorname{Tr}(\rho\log\rho)=-\sum_{j:\lambda_j>0}\lambda_j\log\lambda_j,$$

where $\lambda_j$ are the eigenvalues of $\rho$, the logarithm is natural, and $0\log0:=0$. For any positive semidefinite endomorphisms $X,Y$ on one finite-dimensional $H$, let $\operatorname{supp}X:=(\ker X)^\perp$. Define

$$D(X\|Y):=\operatorname{Tr}(X\log X)-\operatorname{Tr}(X\log Y)$$

when $\operatorname{supp}X\subseteq\operatorname{supp}Y$, taking each logarithm spectrally on its positive support and setting zero-eigenvalue contributions to zero; set $D(X\|Y):=+\infty$ otherwise. For density operators this is the finite-dimensional quantum relative entropy in nats.

For a density operator $\rho_{AB}$ on the ordered product $H_A\otimes H_B$, define $\rho_A:=\operatorname{Tr}_B\rho_{AB}$ and $\rho_B:=\operatorname{Tr}_A\rho_{AB}$, where in orthonormal product bases $\bigl(\operatorname{Tr}_B R\bigr)_{ii'}=\sum_jR_{(i,j),(i',j)}$ and the first factor is retained. Define

$$I(A:B)_\rho:=S(\rho_A)+S(\rho_B)-S(\rho_{AB}).$$

For a density operator $\rho_{ABC}$ on $H_A\otimes H_B\otimes H_C$, define

$$\rho_{AB}:=\operatorname{Tr}_C\rho_{ABC},\qquad \rho_{BC}:=\operatorname{Tr}_A\rho_{ABC},\qquad \rho_B:=\operatorname{Tr}_A(\operatorname{Tr}_C\rho_{ABC}),$$

where each partial trace contracts the indicated tensor factor and retains the other factors in their displayed order.

$$I(A:C\mid B)_\rho:=S(\rho_{AB})+S(\rho_{BC})-S(\rho_B)-S(\rho_{ABC}),$$

using the partial traces in the displayed factor order. For any fixed positive conversion factor $k_B$ with units J/K, the corresponding physical entropy is $S_{\mathrm{phys}}(\rho):=k_BS(\rho)$; no numerical value of $k_B$ is specified here.

For each oriented nearest-neighbor bond $(j,j+1)$, let $h_{j,j+1}=h_{j,j+1}^*$ be an energy operator in joules. These finite local data may be realized on a tensor-product spin space or on a finite fixed-particle site space, provided the stated commutation conditions hold.

The oriented bond current from $j$ to $j+1$ is
$$j_{j,j+1}:=\frac{i}{\hbar}[h_{j,j+1},q_{j+1}].$$
It has unit $\mathsf Q\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$. The total current is the sum over existing bonds, $J_L:=\sum_{(j,j+1)}j_{j,j+1}$, and its Heisenberg evolution for $t\in\mathbb R$ is $J_L(t):=e^{iH_Lt/\hbar}J_Le^{-iH_Lt/\hbar}$. For finite inverse temperature $\beta>0$ in joules$^{-1}$, define $\rho_{\beta,L}:=e^{-\beta H_L}/\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-\beta H_L})$ and $\omega_{\beta,L}(A):=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_{\beta,L}A)$. $$C_L(t):=\frac{1}{L}\operatorname{Re}\,\omega_{\beta,L}\!\left(J_L^\circ(t)J_L^\circ\right)=\frac{1}{2L}\omega_{\beta,L}\!\left(J_L^\circ(t)J_L^\circ+J_L^\circ J_L^\circ(t)\right).$$
The correlation has unit $\mathsf Q^2\,\mathrm{s}^{-2}$ per site.

This definition assigns no transport coefficient by itself. Any proposed finite-volume or thermodynamic transport quantity must additionally state its time cutoff, frequency regulator (for example $e^{-\eta t}$ with $\eta>0$ in seconds$^{-1}$), spatial normalization, and the exact order in which $L\to\infty$, the time cutoff tends to infinity, and any regulator is removed. Fix integers $d,D\ge1$ and a translation invariant tensor $A^1,\ldots,A^d\in M_D(\mathbb C)$ with transfer map $\mathcal E(X):=\sum_iA^iXA^{i*}$. A matrix is positive semidefinite when it is Hermitian with nonnegative quadratic form on every vector. Let $\rho,\ell\in M_D(\mathbb C)$ be positive semidefinite matrices satisfying

$$\operatorname{tr}\rho=1,\qquad \mathcal E(\rho)=\rho,\qquad \mathcal E^*(\ell)=\ell,\qquad \operatorname{tr}(\ell\rho)=1,$$

where $\mathcal E^*(Y):=\sum_iA^{i*}YA^i$, equivalently the trace-pairing adjoint determined by $\operatorname{tr}(Y\mathcal E(X))=\operatorname{tr}(\mathcal E^*(Y)X)$. For a contiguous block of $k\ge1$ sites, write $I=(i_1,\ldots,i_k)$ and $J=(j_1,\ldots,j_k)$ for physical multi-indices, let $e_I$ be its ordered standard product basis, put $O_{I,J}:=\langle Oe_J,e_I\rangle$ for $O\in M_{d^k}(\mathbb C)$, and set $A^I:=A^{i_1}\cdots A^{i_k}$. Define the transfer insertion map and local expectation by

$$\mathcal E_O(X):=\sum_{I,J}O_{I,J}A^JX(A^I)^*,\qquad \omega_k(O):=\operatorname{tr}(\ell\mathcal E_O(\rho)).$$

For any finite nonempty $\Lambda\subset\mathbb Z$ and local observable $O\in\mathcal A_\Lambda$, embed $O$ into the interval $[\min\Lambda,\max\Lambda]$ by inserting identities at missing sites and evaluate the same formula. For the empty region set $\omega_\varnothing(cI):=c$. These definitions give compatible positive normalized local functionals. Their unique density matrices $\rho_\Lambda$ obey $\operatorname{Tr}_{\Lambda'\setminus\Lambda}(\rho_{\Lambda'})=\rho_\Lambda$ whenever $\Lambda\subseteq\Lambda'$. Assume Countable Choice. The transfer-generated infinite-chain state is the unique infinite algebraic state $\omega$ on the norm-completed quasi-local spin algebra whose restriction to every finite region is the defined local functional. No infinite tensor-product Hilbert space is selected.

For observables $O_A\in M_{d^a}(\mathbb C)$ and $O_B\in M_{d^b}(\mathbb C)$ on two fixed consecutive blocks, with $g\ge0$ identity sites between the blocks, the connected correlation is

$$\omega(O_A\otimes I^{\otimes g}\otimes O_B)-\omega(O_A)\omega(O_B).$$

1.1 The finite coefficient sum defining $\mathcal E_O(X)$ is complex-linear in both $O$ and $X$. For $O\ge0$, write its spectral decomposition as $O=\sum_\alpha|v_\alpha\rangle\langle v_\alpha|$, absorbing the square roots of the nonnegative eigenvalues into $v_\alpha$, and put $v_{\alpha,I}=\langle v_\alpha,e_I\rangle$. Then $O_{I,J}=\sum_\alpha v_{\alpha,I}\overline{v_{\alpha,J}}$, so with $K_\alpha:=\sum_J\overline{v_{\alpha,J}}A^J$ the insertion map satisfies $\mathcal E_O(X)=\sum_\alpha K_\alpha X K_\alpha^*\ge0$ whenever $X\ge0$. Diagonalizing $\ell$ by [F7] and expanding $\operatorname{tr}(\ell\mathcal E_O(\rho))$ as a weighted sum of nonnegative diagonal expectations shows $\omega_k(O)\ge0$. For $O=I_{d^k}$, $O_{I,J}=1$ if $I=J$ and $0$ otherwise, so the insertion sums over all length-$k$ words and equals $\mathcal E^k$. The fixed-point equations and $\operatorname{tr}(\ell\rho)=1$ give $\omega_k(I)=\operatorname{tr}(\ell\mathcal E^k(\rho))=1$. Thus each contiguous-block functional is positive and normalized. [given, F1, F7, algebra]

Inserting an identity site on the right composes with $\mathcal E$ on the input, which leaves $\rho$ fixed; inserting one on the left composes with $\mathcal E$ on the output, which leaves the trace pairing with $\ell$ fixed. Repeating these identities shows that the value is independent of the chosen containing interval and that restrictions to nested finite regions agree. The empty-region convention is consistent because every local functional assigns one to the identity. [given, F1, step 1.1, algebra]

$$\widehat W_\gamma(\omega):=\int_{\mathbb R}W_\gamma(t)e^{it\omega}\,dt,$$

such that $\widehat W_\gamma(\omega)=i/\omega$ whenever $|\omega|\ge\gamma$, and for every integer $N\ge0$ there is $c_N<\infty$ with

$$\int_{|t|>T}|W_\gamma(t)|\,dt\le c_N(1+T)^{-N}\qquad(T\ge0).$$

The finite matrix

$$D_\Lambda(s):=\int_{\mathbb R}W_\gamma(t)e^{itH_\Lambda(s)} H_\Lambda'(s)e^{-itH_\Lambda(s)}\,dt$$

is self-adjoint and satisfies

$$P_\Lambda'(s)=i[D_\Lambda(s),P_\Lambda(s)].$$

1.1 Define $\chi(\omega)=e\exp(-1/(1-(\omega/\gamma)^2))$ for $|\omega|<\gamma$, and $\chi(\omega)=0$ otherwise. The exponential tends to zero faster than every power at the endpoints, so $\chi$ is real, even, smooth, compactly supported in $[-\gamma,\gamma]$, and $\chi(0)=1$. Define $w(t)=(2\pi)^{-1}\int\chi(\omega)e^{-it\omega}\,d\omega$. By [A1], [F3], and the sign/scale conversion stated in [F3], $w$ is Schwartz, real and even, its Fourier transform $\widehat w(\omega)=\int w(t)e^{it\omega}dt$ equals $\chi(\omega)$, and $\int w=1$. For $t>0$ put $W_\gamma(t)=\int_t^\infty w(v)\,dv$; for $t<0$ put $W_\gamma(t)=-\int_{-\infty}^t w(v)\,dv$; set $W_\gamma(0)=0$. Evenness and unit integral make $W_\gamma$ odd with one-sided limits $W_\gamma(0^\pm)=\pm\frac12$. For every $N$, a Schwartz bound $|w(v)|\le c(1+|v|)^{-N-2}$ on either tail gives $|W_\gamma(t)|\le c'(1+|t|)^{-N-1}$; hence $W_\gamma\in L^1$ and has the stated tail estimate. Integration by parts on the two half-lines, accounting for the jump of size $1$ at zero and using $W_\gamma'=-w$ away from zero, gives $-\widehat w(\omega)=-1-i\omega\widehat W_\gamma(\omega)$. $$C_G:=\sup_{x,y\in\Gamma} \frac{\sum_{z\in\Gamma}G(d_\infty(x,z))G(d_\infty(z,y))} {G(d_\infty(x,y))},$$

where $C_F$ uses this same formula with the base weight $F=F_{d+1}$. Each such constant is finite and positive. In particular, for all $x,y\in\Gamma$,

$$\sum_{z\in\Gamma}G(d_\infty(x,z))G(d_\infty(z,y)) \le C_G\,G(d_\infty(x,y)).$$

The constant $C_{F_a}$ may be taken to be the convolution constant $C_F$ of $F$, independently of $a$.
